slides.texte_overlay:
How to make your memory
Ridiculously good
Write it by hand. Notes taken with a pen are remembered better than typed ones, because your brain has to summarise.
Use stories. Turn facts into a short story or a funny picture in your mind. Strange images are much easier to remember.
Exercise regularly. Running, cycling, swimming. Moving your body helps your brain stay sharp and form new memories.
Learn in short sessions. Twenty focused minutes, then a break. Your brain remembers the start and end of each session best.
Feed your memory daily. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and small daily lessons stick better than long sessions.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Small daily lessons stick better than long sessions.

slides.texte_overlay: Reduce multitasking. Doing one thing at a time helps your brain store it properly. Focus on one task.
Test yourself before bed. A quick review in the evening helps your brain keep it while you sleep. Two minutes is enough.
